extracted.intended_audience: MathML implementers, renderer authors, XML/HTML authors, and tool authors validating or producing MathML 4
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative requirements from the MathML 4 specification for serializing, validating, and rendering MathML (Presentation, Content, Strict Content, Full, and Legacy). Intended to inform implementers about grammar locations, namespace usage, attribute constraints, validation, and operator-spacing defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance to MathML 4 grammars
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the specified MathML 4 grammars for the relevant serialization: Presentation MathML, Strict Content MathML, Content MathML, Full MathML, and Legacy MathML (each provided as Relax NG files and referenced URLs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grammar files are normative sources (e.g. mathml4-presentation.rnc, mathml4-strict-content.rnc, mathml4-content.rnc, mathml4.rnc, mathml4-legacy.rnc). Implementations should build on these grammars and follow the element/attribute productions they define.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default MathML namespace
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML documents/serializations should use the MathML namespace as the default: m = "http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set the default namespace for MathML elements to avoid ambiguity and match the specification's namespace declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid namespace prefixes in XML serialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the MathML DTD supports a strategy allowing namespace prefixes, the specification recommends that namespace prefixes are not used in XML serialization of MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting namespace prefixes improves compatibility with the HTML serialization of MathML and is the recommended practice for XML-serialized MathML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character entity usage in XML serialization
rubrics_metrics.description: In XML serialization, character entity references such as ∫ may not be used unless a DTD is specified (either the full MathML DTD or the set of HTML/MathML entity declarations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer using the character directly (e.g. ∫) or a numeric character reference (e.g. ∫) in XML MathML unless you include the appropriate DTD/entity declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation with XML Schema (XSD) and its limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML fragments can be validated using the provided XML Schema (mathml4.xsd), but that schema was mechanically generated and omits constraints that cannot be enforced using XSD syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the XSD for basic validation but be aware that some Relax NG constraints will not be checked by XSD; rely on the Relax NG grammars for full validation where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator dictionary as normative defaults for spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification provides an operator dictionary for rendering properties (spacing, form, priority) of operator/fence/separator/accent elements (mo elements); implementations of the MathML Core will use these values as normative defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look up operator entries by element content plus the form attribute value. Use the dictionary entries as the default operator spacing rules unless overridden by other presentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: lspace and rspace encoding (units and range)
rubrics_metrics.description: Values for the lspace and rspace attributes range from 0 to 7, denoting multiples of 1/18 em matching the values used for namedspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When mapping or interpreting lspace/rspace use the 0–7 scale where each unit is 1/18em; implementers should respect these discrete values to match the spec's spacing model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-sensitive spacing for invisible operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Spacing for invisible operators (InvisibleTimes and ApplyFunction) should be chosen context-sensitively rather than purely statically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For <mo>⁡</mo> (e.g., sin x) the total spacing (lspace + rspace) should be greater than zero in contexts like 'sin x' where the right operand doesn't start with a fence. For <mo>⁢</mo> the total spacing should be greater than zero when both operands (or nearest baseline tokens) are multi-character identifiers displayed in a non-slanted font. Implementations should apply contextual heuristics for these operators rather than fixed zero spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing behavior in scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Renderers may choose to use no spacing for most operators that appear in scripts (sub/superscripts or other script positions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a permitted implementation optimization: spacing rules that apply on the main baseline can be relaxed in script-level contexts to improve visual compactness, but do so consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy MathML support and deprecated constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML 4 removes some elements and attributes deprecated in MathML 3; the Legacy MathML schema extends MathML 4 to reintroduce those constructs for validating existing documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If validating or supporting legacy documents, use the mathml4-legacy.rnc which restores removed elements/attributes and provides deprecated attribute variants; for new content prefer the non-legacy MathML 4 constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to element-specific attribute enumerations and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Each MathML element has specified allowed attributes, attribute types, and enumerated values (e.g., mfrac.numalign/denomalign, mstyle's scriptsizemultiplier/decimalpoint/align options, mtable's columnwidth/columnalign, mtd rowspan/columnspan numeric types, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations and authors must conform to the attribute names, allowed value sets, and types/patterns declared for each element in the grammar (many attributes reference types such as mathml-boolean, length-percentage, positive-integer, xsd:anyURI, etc.). Follow the provided enumerations and patterns to ensure valid MathML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of presentation vs. content/strict-content distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification separates Presentation MathML, Strict Content MathML, Content MathML, and combinations (Full MathML); the Presentation grammar builds on the MathML Core and the Content grammar builds on Strict Content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct grammar subset for your use case (presentation vs content semantics). For semantic/expressive content use Content/Strict Content; for purely visual layout use Presentation. Full MathML merges these as needed.
